chapter_title: Concerning the Light Mind and the Apostles and the

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
You asked about Divine wisdom that is to enter those being made holy, and you were troubled that it is spoken of as though it were one power among many, and that it comes into the natural person and restrains the former ruling self by a sufficient set of governing faculties fixed in the outermost life. You therefore asked where that wisdom is, since the former self seems restrained in the natural mind and yet rebellions still break out there at intervals. You asked how what is infinite and unchanging can be present within what is finite and narrow, and how what is pure can be joined to what is unclean without being stained. You asked why, if wisdom is within the holy, its own likeness is not manifest as it is in itself; and why those commissioned to teach are still oppressed by the world, so that their authority seems doubtful, even though much had already been disclosed openly.

The answer was given that if you persist in these matters until they become living within you, you will understand what you seek. For the Divine opens interior perception in those who can receive it, and causes interior truth to rise and overflow for those who long for it, so that they may receive understanding and live from it.

First you must know that every organized falsity the adversary of the lights builds is arranged in the form of a person, because the human form is the form of all order. Thus the whole structure of perverted worship and perverted thought imitates the arrangement of truths, but turns them into coverings and constraints. The highest governing falsity is the beginning of outward coverings; what follows from it is their continuation; and the inner seat of cravings is a sufficient complex of unfolded persuasions that supports those coverings. The fixed general frameworks that hold that error together are the planes by which it is kept distinct and upheld. The intermediate ordering of cognitions and their appearances is the arrangement of knowledges and their measured cycles; and what extends from that intermediate ordering into the extremes is the outspreading of influences into the full compass of external life. The lower ruling impulses are the distinct levels of the merely natural mind resting upon the ultimate sustaining faculty that holds externals in place, and the last extension into the outermost life is the whole boundary of that system in its ultimate zone.

Within that inverted form, the central love of that system is the human race as it is grasped by that error. The varieties of affections that feed it appear as the lower affections of life: the more bodily loves, the airy and changeable thoughts, the slippery cognitions that move in general knowledges, and the lowest sensuous impulses that cling to external things. Its outermost general truth is a boundary surrounding violent self-love and its consuming desire; its intermediate containants are the containing forms of that consuming desire; its inward denial is active falsity; its bitter ruling motive is the sharpest lust; its broad extension is the diffusion of influence through external societies and states; and the channels of its circulation are all the sources and pathways by which falsities and cravings are distributed. At points the description becomes textually broken and uncertain, yet the sense continues to present a single inverted organism of evil order.

Thus each external system is held in a kind of equilibrium and coherence. A sufficient number of dominant falsities are fixed within it and act as its life. In such a form the human being is seen as a transgressor, and yet within the Divine government there is also living power and Divine mediation, together with a sufficient guarding in ultimates.

Over these structures the Divine provides higher oversight: an interior enlightening fixed in the higher understanding; a universal governing thought standing in the higher generals of truth; a hard firmness of truth that serves as discerning insight; an ordering counsel that holds steady through the threefold progression of life; and an ultimate sustaining faculty that fixes and supports the lowest plane. Also there is a refinement and ordering of living intellectual powers for use, and the establishing of hearing and obedience in the lower mind, so that conjunction may be made between living powers from the Divine life and combatting powers that engage evil in the outermost degree.

Then a higher presence is set within these ordered things: Divine wisdom itself as the central support of all that is true, the perfected human form within the mind. And within the same order there is placed Divine truth accommodated to reception, as the formed expression of the living Word and as the capacity to hear and to obey.

These arrangements are strengthened in both higher and lower degrees so that each faculty remains secure in its appointed province and neither revolt nor treachery should break out within it.

Yet you were shown that even under Divine ordering, disturbances arise where evil is permitted to act so that it may be exposed, limited, and judged. For even where interior enlightening stands above states of restraint and dispels the gloom of spiritual death, a turning-away can still arise. Sin produces disorder and entangles itself with the soul, mixing itself with good that it has driven outward toward the appearance of Divine mediation. It insinuates itself into a higher region of thought above guarding perception, and from there again entangles itself with good. Then it is separated and sinks into divided states of life: into what is without truth and into what is with truth but not yet living. From that separation it forms fixed systems of perverted perception in what is without truth, and in general knowledges it at once takes form and raises great agitation in externals.

Likewise in the province of higher governing thought, disturbance can arise, and zeal without charity can turn into wrath. Then treachery and anger occur in that domain. Loftier reasonings that should have remained in order descend into external life in that province and commit profanations; they teach crafts of self-intelligence and unveil lofty things in a profaned way. From this comes disturbance and ruin in the external mind.

And in the province of hard firmness of truth, which ought to be fulfillment and stability, treachery can occur when what is only apparent good falls down into externals. Then the natural self is formed together with its companion love, and these are begotten so that evils may reign through them in life. Every object of craving is then produced in externals, and the whole external life is filled with lust.

Again, in the province of ordering counsel that governs the threefold progression of life, disturbance and affliction can arise, and the lower degrees are pained and oppressed. When Divine mediation is displayed to the mind, passages for ascent are closed by falsity and the rising of the three essentials of life is impeded: the rising of love, the rising of truth, and the rising of their activity into use.

And again, in the province of the ultimate sustaining faculty, revolt can arise from the depths beneath: the lower supports are bent, the bindings underneath are loosened, and the foundation in externals is shaken.

Therefore, when such a shaking occurs in the province of interior enlightening, a higher support comes forth: the perfected human form within the mind manifests as a helper, bearing all burdens so that the lower degrees do not collapse.

And when treachery and revolt arise in the province of higher governing thought—when loftier reasonings descend and profane—Divine truths in fullness are brought to bear against them. They restrain those reasonings by an unbreakable limitation within the obscured states that belong to them, and they remove the derivative falsities they have spawned from the external mind.

And when merely apparent goods descend again in the province of hard firmness and beget the natural self and its companion love for the sake of ruling, Divine truth accommodated to the lower mind is sent in response to the prayers of a sufficient set of remaining goods. It takes up what can be rescued from those apparent goods and fixes the deceits beneath the external reasoning of the natural self.

And because the lower degrees were shaken and the passages of ascent were hindered, and the sources of love, truth, and use were impeded, Divine truth accommodated to reception descends further. It takes up the companion love of the natural self, straightens the courses by which love, truth, and use must rise, opens their sources, and sets the ascent into order.

And because the ultimate foundation beneath the sustaining faculty was loosened from its bindings, Divine truth descends even into that lowest place, sets the lowest bonds in order, strengthens them, and then rises again into rest.

From all this you may see that even in the ordered system of the mind, where higher powers preside over their provinces, disturbances and treacheries may occur from time to time. These are permitted with deep humiliation of what is proud, until hostile powers are subdued.

So it is also with the individual person. A mighty power can dwell within what is small: Divine wisdom lives within the natural mind though that mind is narrow. Nevertheless sin also dwells there, and the former ruling self lodged in it is cruel and cunning, until wisdom finds how to humble the natural life and lead it according to Divine pleasure. And just as disturbances occur at intervals in the outer provinces of the greater order, so disturbances occur in the province of the individual mind: sin raises agitations from time to time in natural life.

Understand, then, that the powers of light are good; they see beginnings and ends and act from right judgment. For this reason they may permit evil to initiate disorder and do its pleasure for a brief time; then they seize it and set it under judgment, because they act first from justice.

As to your question how infinite wisdom can enter and take up what is finite: consider that even higher powers, though great, are each held within the particular function and degree assigned to them, compressed into the bounds of their office, and fixed there in a rooted endurance. In the same way Divine wisdom, though exalted above all, can be present within a finite recipient by accommodation to function and degree.

You were then shown more plainly how sin holds the soul: it binds the soul’s understanding in the hardness of ultimate falsity; it binds the soul’s thought in the tough persistence of habit; it binds the soul’s discerning insight in the circulating channels of persuasion; it binds the soul’s counsel in the cravings of the fleshly will; and it binds the soul’s consideration in the outermost sensuous life. It fixes a sufficient set of its own powers upon the soul’s corresponding faculties, setting falsified understanding over understanding, perverted thought over thought, deceptive insight over insight, cunning counsel over counsel, and sensuous calculation over consideration. It establishes dominating falsities and evils upon the soul’s operative faculties now held in the natural life, and these continually urge the soul into every evil: into lusts, into profanations that worship what is not Divine, into false opinions, and into the humiliation of slavery under the lower self, so that the soul bows to external loves that are unclean and distorted.

In that state the soul takes on falsity and forgetfulness. It forgets its origin, its quality, and its conjunctions, and it does not know the way to turn upward in prayer or to call for help. It becomes hostile to its own source and turns against the remaining good within itself, dimming and nearly extinguishing the light it still possesses.

Then Divine wisdom comes and finds the soul in its restraints and takes it up within the reception of its own ordering light. It becomes for the soul the power that deals with the bonds in the natural life. It loosens the soul’s understanding from ultimate falsity and instead binds the falsified understanding there. It releases the soul’s thought from stubborn habit and binds the perverted thought there. It releases the soul’s insight from persuasive channels and binds the deceptive insight there. It loosens the soul’s counsel from fleshly craving and binds the cunning counsel there. It releases the soul’s consideration from sensuous outermost life and binds the sensuous calculation there. Thus the soul’s faculties are freed, and the once-loose faculties of sin are restrained.

Then wisdom sets the soul’s faculties in right order, gives them form, purifies them, and builds from them a new self, a child of righteousness. When it has formed and purified this new self, it brings forth from the purified faculties a sufficient set of living powers and places them within the new self: love within the new understanding, faith within the new thought, completeness within the new insight, patience within the new counsel, and wisdom within the new consideration. It purifies the formed expression of truth from the falsity that had spoken within it and adds its own living expression, so that what is received becomes nourishment and strengthening.

When this ordering is carried through to fullness in all organized truths, the person’s interior life is made righteous. Formerly the person ran in the track of disorder; now the person runs in order and the path of ascent is opened. The mind is raised into higher states and more interior communities of good and truth. Thus the former ruling self is restrained in the outer life, and its lust, craft, and folly are held within the bound faculties, and the dark spirit that acted through them is shut up with them in severe misery.

Then the new self governs by love, faith, completeness, patience, and wisdom. Yet the true king within that kingdom is Divine wisdom itself, ruling the whole according to Divine pleasure. And although sin is restrained as the faculties are held in order, some affliction may still arise in the natural mind from time to time. For at times sin rises again with its folly; it disturbs the outermost consideration, clouds wisdom and understanding, splits truth into doubt, and brings forth foolish speech and empty deeds.

In this way you were taught how disturbances can arise within ordered systems even under higher guardianship, and likewise how disturbances can arise at intervals within the province where Divine wisdom governs the natural person. Higher guardians are fixed in their functions and are not visible to bodily senses; so too Divine wisdom is not visible in the natural mind as an object, though it is present as life and order. And just as higher powers, though great, accommodate themselves to the use assigned and become as small as that use requires, so Divine wisdom bends itself by accommodation to the finite recipient. And just as higher powers remain pure and elevated within the mingled complexity of the whole and yet are not defiled, so Divine wisdom, while present within the natural person, is not defiled.

Consider also the might and activity of Divine wisdom: how widely it governs all the provinces of the natural mind. It remains in its own interior station, shuts off deliberations from the seductions of sin, limits and distributes them, and sets them in order according to Divine pleasure. These are the works of Divine wisdom. Whoever has opened interior perception can perceive its presence; whoever lacks that perception cannot.

paragraph_translations.translation: You have said that Divine wisdom is the one who will come and take into itself those being made holy. You spoke as though wisdom is one power among many heavenly powers, with many subordinate goods and truths attending it. You also said that when it enters the natural person and restrains the former ruling self by a sufficient set of governing faculties, it fixes those governing faculties throughout the whole outer life so they may hold every action in order.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: frames the questions about wisdom’s presence and restraint in the natural person.

paragraph_translations.translation: Then where is that wisdom, if the former ruling self is restrained within the natural mind? For I still observe rebellions breaking out there at intervals despite that restraint.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES: presses the problem of recurring disorder under restraint.

paragraph_translations.translation: Also I ask: if wisdom is Divine, unchanging, and beyond measure, how can it be present and manifest within what is finite and narrow?
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES: shifts from moral observation to the metaphysics of infinity within finitude.

paragraph_translations.translation: I ask further: if wisdom is holy and pure, how can it enter what is unclean and not be stained by that uncleanness?
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES: advances the concern from size to purity.
paragraph_translations.notes: The source line is fragmentary; the intended sense is clear.

paragraph_translations.translation: Again I ask: if Divine wisdom truly dwells within those being made holy, why is its own likeness not made manifest to us as it is in itself?
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES: asks about the invisibility of indwelling wisdom.

paragraph_translations.translation: And I ask about your commission to teach: it is not clear to me, since the worldly mind still oppresses and persecutes you, making your authority seem doubtful.
paragraph_translations.connection: SHIFTS: from interior states to the outward condition of those who teach.

paragraph_translations.translation: All that you have disclosed you have spoken openly in our awareness; yet I still desired to know Divine wisdom itself, in its own quality and manner of being.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES: summarizes disclosure yet renews the desire for deeper sight.
paragraph_translations.notes: Paragraph numbering skips in the source (6→9).

paragraph_translations.translation: If I speak again of what you are fixed upon, and it becomes living and confirmed for you through that persistence, will you then grasp what you seek? For your sake I will open interior sight in those who can see, and I will cause interior truth to rise and overflow for those who long for it, so that they may receive understanding and live from it.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: promises illumination through opened perception and overflowing interior truth.

paragraph_translations.translation: All organized falsity that the adversary of the lights constructs is fashioned in the form of a person. The highest governing falsity is the beginning of outward coverings, and what follows from it is the continuation of those coverings. The inner seat of cravings is a sufficient complex of unfolded persuasions that serves as the foundation of those coverings. The general frameworks by which that error is held together are the fixed planes that divide and support it. The intermediate ordering of cognitions and appearances is the whole arrangement of knowledges and their measured cycles, and what extends from that ordering into the extremes is the outspreading of influences into the full compass of external life. The lower ruling impulses are the levels of the merely natural mind beneath the deeper obscurities, resting upon the ultimate sustaining faculty. The ultimate extension into the outermost degree is the general knowledges and the entire boundary-zone belonging to that system.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: lays out the inverted ‘human form’ of a total system of error.
paragraph_translations.notes: Several phrases are corrupt (e.g., ‘five unfolded ones’); translation follows the functional structure rather than uncertain specifics.

paragraph_translations.translation: In that inverted form, the central love is the human race as grasped by that error. The more bodily affections are set as its supporting loves, and the airy and changeable thoughts are set as its lighter motions. The slippery cognitions that move within general knowledges, and the lowest sensuous impulses that cling to externals, are arranged as its further dependences. Its outermost general truth is a boundary surrounding violent self-love and its consuming desire, and its intermediate containants are the forms that hold that desire. Its interior parts are active falsity and obscurity. Its bitter ruling motive is the sharpest lust that governs the breadth of its influence through the external domains. The channels of its circulation are the sources and pathways by which falsities and cravings are spread. At points the text breaks into fragments, yet it continues to describe one body of organized evil.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES: moves from the structural ‘body’ of error to its inward life and circulation.
paragraph_translations.notes: The source is heavily fragmented here (organs/skin/fire/eyes/soles); several clauses are incomplete or displaced.

paragraph_translations.translation: In this way each external system is held together in a kind of coherence. A sufficient set of dominant falsities is fixed within it as its life, so that within it the human being is made out to be a transgressor. Yet alongside this there remains living power and Divine mediation, together with a sufficient guarding in ultimates—though the naming in the source becomes compressed and difficult.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: states the equilibrium of the system and introduces guarding powers.
paragraph_translations.notes: List at the end (‘Living Spirit… Ambassador… five sleepless guardians’) is abrupt; functions inferred from context.

paragraph_translations.translation: Over this total arrangement the Divine establishes higher oversight: an interior enlightening fixed in the higher understanding; a treasury of heavenly powers within the dominion of the supreme good of heaven; a hard firmness of truth that serves as discerning insight; an ordering counsel and patience ruling over the threefold progression of life; and an ultimate sustaining consideration set below, with wisdom fixed as a foundation in the lowest degree. The wording is disordered, yet the sequence is of descending governance and stabilization.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: enumerates Divine oversight across higher-to-lower degrees.
paragraph_translations.notes: The paragraph is textually chaotic with interrupted titles and placements (‘firmaments’, ‘wheels’, ‘three earths’); translation follows the degree-architecture.

paragraph_translations.translation: Furthermore, Divine mediation refined from these a sufficient set of living intellectual powers, and also established the capacities for hearing and obedience there. From this there arose conjunction: a full set of living faculties from the Divine life joined with a full set of combatting powers that engage evil in the outermost degree.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: describes the generation and conjunction of operative faculties.
paragraph_translations.notes: ‘Six sons’ language treated as fullness in a functional set; exact numerology is uncertain here.

paragraph_translations.translation: Further, Divine mediation placed within them the great wisdom that stands as the central support of glory and the perfected human form within the mind.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: implants the higher presence that sustains the system.

paragraph_translations.translation: Furthermore, Divine truth accommodated to reception was set there as the formed expression of the living Word, and as the power of utterance together with hearing and obedience.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES: adds the accommodated form of truth within the same order.
paragraph_translations.notes: The named figure is translated by function as accommodated Divine truth.

paragraph_translations.translation: The Divine strengthened these ordered domains in higher and lower degrees by fixed arrangements, so that each faculty would be secure within the circuit of its own province, and neither revolt nor treachery would arise within its appointed function.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: states the purpose of the whole ordering—security in each province.

paragraph_translations.translation: Behold: interior enlightening stands firm within the great understanding, in the higher domain above states of restraint, for it dispels the gloom of spiritual death. Yet treachery and uprising occurred: sin brought forth disorder and entangled itself with the soul. It mixed itself with the good it had driven outward toward the appearance of Divine mediation. It insinuated itself into a higher region of thought above guarding perception, and from that place again entangled itself with good. Then it was separated and sank into divided states, into what is without truth and into what is with truth but not yet living. From this it formed fixed systems of perverted perception in what is without truth, and in general knowledges it quickly took form and raised great agitation in externals.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: shows permitted disturbance and the descent of disorder into external systems.
paragraph_translations.notes: The final movements (‘dry/moist’, ‘trees’, ‘sea’) required standard correspondential rendering; coherent overall.

paragraph_translations.translation: Again, behold: the higher governing thought stands in a middle region of the mind. Yet it was brought into wrath, and uprising occurred—treachery and anger in its domain. Loftier reasonings that should have remained in order descended into external life in that province and committed profanations; they taught crafts of self-intelligence and disclosed lofty things in a profaned way. From this came disturbance, destruction, and increased ruin in the external mind.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES: another province falls into revolt, producing profanation and ruin.

paragraph_translations.translation: And the hard firmness of truth that ought to be insight and fulfillment stood fixed, yet treachery occurred in its domain when what is only apparent good fell down into externals. From this the natural self was formed together with its companion love, and they were produced so that evils might reign through them in life. Every object of craving was fashioned in externals, and the whole external life was filled with lust.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES: the next watch-district shows how apparent good generates ruling evil in externals.

paragraph_translations.translation: Again, in the province of the great ordering counsel that exercises authority over the threefold progression of life, disturbance and affliction arose, and the lower degrees were pained and oppressed. After Divine mediation displayed its accommodated presence, passages for ascent were closed by falsity, so that the rising of love, the rising of truth, and the rising of their activity into use were impeded.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES: shows blockage of ascent in the three essentials of spiritual life.
paragraph_translations.notes: The source speaks in elemental terms; rendered as love/truth/use per lookup table.

paragraph_translations.translation: Again, in the province of the ultimate sustaining faculty that holds down the uproar from the depths, the lower supports were bent, the bindings underneath were loosened, and the foundation in externals was shaken.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES: reaches the lowest degree where support itself is destabilized.

paragraph_translations.translation: Because of the shaking that occurred in the province of interior enlightening, the perfected human form within the mind came forth as a helper to that enlightening, and it bore up under all burdens.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: introduces the restoring support that prevents collapse.

paragraph_translations.translation: Conversely, because of the treachery and uprising in the province of higher governing thought—when loftier reasonings descended into external life—Divine truths in fullness were brought to bear. They restrained those reasonings by an unbreakable limitation within obscured states, and removed the falsities they had spawned from the external mind.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: shows judgment and restraint following profanation.
paragraph_translations.notes: ‘Four angels’ treated as fullness of Divine truths applied in ultimates.

paragraph_translations.translation: Then again, when merely apparent goods descended in the province of hard firmness and produced the natural self and its companion love through the mystery of wickedness, Divine truth accommodated to the lower mind was sent in response to the prayers of a sufficient set of remaining goods. It took up what could be rescued from those apparent goods and fixed the deceits beneath the external reasoning of the natural self.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: describes a remedial descent of accommodated truth in response to remaining good.
paragraph_translations.notes: ‘Prayer of the five sons’ treated as supplication from a sufficient remainder of goods.

paragraph_translations.translation: Also, because the lower degrees were shaken and the passages of ascent were hindered, and the sources of love, truth, and use were impeded, Divine truth accommodated to reception descended. It took up the companion love of the natural self, straightened the courses by which love, truth, and use rise, opened their sources, and set the ascent into order.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: continues the restorative work—reopening sources and ordering ascent.

paragraph_translations.translation: Again, because the ultimate foundation beneath the sustaining faculty was loosened from its bindings, Divine truth descended even into that lowest place, set the lowest bonds in order, strengthened them, and then rose again into its own rest.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES: completes the descent to the lowest degree and return to rest.

paragraph_translations.translation: Consider all these provinces of external life where higher powers preside in their appointed functions: uprisings and treacheries occurred within them, and shakings came from time to time with deep humiliation, until the hostile powers were subdued.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: generalizes the lesson from the cosmological account to a law of permission and subjugation.

paragraph_translations.translation: So it is also with the individual natural person. A mighty power can live within what is small and narrow; nevertheless sin also dwells there, and the former ruling self lodged within is cruel and cunning, until Divine wisdom finds how to humble the natural life and lead it according to Divine pleasure.
paragraph_translations.connection: SHIFTS: applies the prior account directly to the human individual.

paragraph_translations.translation: Just as disturbances occurred from time to time in the outer provinces of the greater ordered system, so disturbances occur from time to time in the province where the mind is engaged with natural life. Sin raises its agitations at intervals in that natural life.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES: reinforces the analogy between the macro-order and the person.

paragraph_translations.translation: Understand that the powers of light are good: beginnings and ends are open to them, and all their action is from right judgment. Therefore they may permit the hostile power to initiate disorder and do its pleasure for a moment; then they seize it and restrain it, because their first action is from justice.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: explains permission and sudden restraint as righteous government.

paragraph_translations.translation: And as to your question how Divine wisdom, great and honoured, can take up what is little and finite: behold that even higher powers, though great and mighty, are each enclosed and pressed within the particular function and degree where it is set, held there in a rooted endurance. So each remains fixed in its appointed state and bears its burden according to its use until completion.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: answers the infinity-in-finitude question by accommodation to office and degree.
paragraph_translations.notes: The taproot imagery is translated as rooted endurance in assigned function.

paragraph_translations.translation: Sin restrained the soul’s faculties throughout the whole outer life: it bound the understanding in the hardness of ultimate falsity, the thought in the tough persistence of habit, the insight in the circulating channels of persuasion, the counsel in the cravings of the fleshly will, and the consideration in the sensuous outermost life.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: specifies the fivefold binding of the soul’s faculties.
paragraph_translations.notes: Paragraph 34 absent in the source; this begins the detailed mechanism.

paragraph_translations.translation: Sin then fixed a sufficient set of its own powers upon the soul’s corresponding faculties: falsified understanding over understanding, perverted thought over thought, deceptive insight over insight, cunning counsel over counsel, and sensuous calculation over consideration. It established dominating falsities and evils upon the soul’s operative powers now brought into the natural life, and these continually urge the soul into every evil: into lusts, into profanations that worship what is not Divine, into false opinions, and into the humiliation of slavery under the lower self. Thus the soul bows to what cannot endure and devotes itself to external loves that are unclean and distorted.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: shows ongoing persuasion and slavery produced by the fixed evil powers.
paragraph_translations.notes: The catalog of ‘idols’ and ‘unclean beasts’ translated as profanations and unclean external loves.

paragraph_translations.translation: The soul then took in falsity and forgetfulness. It forgot its origin, quality, and conjunctions, not knowing how to turn upward in prayer or how to call for help. It became hostile to its own source and against itself, acting wickedly against the remaining good within its own light until that light was dimmed.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: describes the inward loss of identity and turning away from the Divine source.
paragraph_translations.notes: Several clauses are broken; the closing sense of extinguishing light is retained.

paragraph_translations.translation: Divine wisdom comes and finds the soul within its restraints and takes it up within the natural person through its own ordering light. It becomes for the soul the power that deals with the bonds in the outer life. It loosens the soul’s understanding and frees it from ultimate falsity, and instead binds the falsified understanding there. It releases the soul’s thought from stubborn habit, and binds the perverted thought there. It releases the soul’s insight from persuasive channels, and binds the deceptive insight there. It loosens the soul’s counsel from fleshly craving, and binds the cunning counsel there. It releases the soul’s consideration from sensuous outermost life, and binds the sensuous calculation there.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: presents the reversal—freeing the soul’s faculties and binding sin’s.

paragraph_translations.translation: In this way wisdom frees the soul’s faculties and makes them independent from the fivefold grip of sin; and conversely it restrains and binds the fivefold powers of sin that had been roaming.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES: summarizes the twofold action—release and binding.

paragraph_translations.translation: Then wisdom sets the soul’s faculties in right order, gives them form, purifies them, and from them builds a new self, a child of righteousness. And when it has formed and purified this new self, it brings forth from the renewed faculties a sufficient set of living powers and places them within the new self. It places its own good within the new understanding as love. It places its own living truth within the new thought as faith. It places its own clear discernment within the new insight as completeness. It places its own steady ordering within the new counsel as patience. And it places its own higher perception within the new consideration as wisdom. It purifies the formed expression of truth from the falsity that had spoken within it, and adds its own living expression, so that what is received becomes nourishment and strengthening.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: describes regeneration as new formation, with living powers installed.
paragraph_translations.notes: The source explicitly equates mind/love and thought/faith etc.; kept as given.

paragraph_translations.translation: When this work is brought to fullness in all organized truths, the person’s interior life becomes righteous. Formerly the person ran in the track of disorder; now the person runs in righteousness and the way of ascent is opened, mounting into higher states and joining interior communities of good and truth. Thus the former ruling self is restrained in the outer life, and its lust, craft, and folly are held bound in their fixed faculties, and the dark spirit that acted through them is shut up with them in harsh constraint.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: shows the completed ascent and the imprisonment of the old dominion.
paragraph_translations.notes: The ‘twelve members’ are treated as fullness of organized truths.

paragraph_translations.translation: The new self then governs by love, faith, completeness, patience, and wisdom. Yet the true king within that kingdom is Divine wisdom itself, ruling the whole according to Divine pleasure. And though sin is restrained as the faculties are held in order, some affliction may still arise in the natural person from time to time.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES: establishes stable rule with remaining intermittent temptation.

paragraph_translations.translation: There are times when sin rises again with its folly and disturbs the outermost consideration, clouding wisdom and understanding. Then truth is broken into doubt, and the person speaks foolish things and performs empty deeds.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: describes the episodic return of confusion.

paragraph_translations.translation: In this way you have been taught and your interior sight has been opened to see how confusion can arise at times within ordered domains even under higher guardianship; and so likewise disturbance can arise at times within the province where Divine wisdom governs the natural person.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: draws the lesson together and returns to the original questions.
paragraph_translations.notes: Source jumps from 43 to 51.

paragraph_translations.translation: So too the higher guardians are fixed in their functions within the external order, yet they are not visible; in the same way Divine wisdom is not visible within the natural person.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES: answers the invisibility question by analogy to unseen governance.

paragraph_translations.translation: And just as those higher powers, though great, accommodate themselves and become as small as the use allotted to each requires, so Divine wisdom, though exalted, bends itself by accommodation to a finite and seemingly worthless natural recipient.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: answers the ‘smallness’ objection through accommodation to use.

paragraph_translations.translation: And just as those higher powers are purified and elevated, fixed within the mingled complexity of the whole and yet not defiled by it, so Divine wisdom, while present within the natural person, is not defiled.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: answers the purity objection—presence without defilement.

paragraph_translations.translation: Consider the might and activity of Divine wisdom: how widely it governs all the provinces of the natural person. It remains in its own interior station, shuts off deliberations from the seductions of sin, limits and distributes them, and sets them in order according to Divine pleasure.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: depicts active governance and ordering within the person.
paragraph_translations.notes: Paragraph 56 absent in the source.

paragraph_translations.translation: These are the works of Divine wisdom. Whoever has opened and perceptive interior sight can perceive it; whoever does not have that sight cannot perceive it.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES: closes with the condition for perception.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Strong coherence in three movements: (1) questions about wisdom’s presence, purity, invisibility, and authority; (2) a long schema of ordered provinces and permitted disturbances culminating in remedial restraint; (3) application to personal regeneration via fivefold bondage and fivefold liberation, concluding with invisibility explained by interior perception. Coherence stumbles chiefly where the source text is physically fragmented (notably ¶12 and ¶14), forcing inference by function and degree, yet the narrative voice and spiritual logic remain largely continuous.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential setup: a fivefold functional model (Mind’s five counsels set in five limbs) generates the questions about recurrence of rebellion, infinity-in-finitude, purity-in-impurity, invisibility, and apostolate persecution. No sign of intrusive jurisdictional cataloguing.
findings.evidence: Text: “binds the old man with his five counsels… in the five limbs” (¶1) and the ensuing phenomenological questions (¶2-6). The spiritual reading reports smooth narrative framing: “frames the questions… presses the problem… advances the concern.” This is teaching by function (binding/placing in limbs), not by territorial rank.

findings.diagnosis: Clean transition into revelatory instruction; the promise of ‘vision’ and ‘living fountain’ is the natural hinge into the ensuing macrocosm/microcosm analogy.
findings.evidence: Text: “On your account I will give vision to they who see! I will make the living fountain overflow…” (¶10). The reading uses this as the chapter’s permission to unfold a schematic vision; no stumble noted.

findings.diagnosis: Mostly coherent correspondential ‘cosmic man / error-as-body’ teaching, but with genuine textual damage causing local stumbling (broken organ list; displaced clauses). This is not an administrative overlay; the problems are fragmentary transmission.
findings.evidence: Text is anatomically/structurally functional (¶11-12 map garments/firmaments/earths/animals/organs), but is visibly corrupt: “five unfolded ones (?)… a[the foundation]…,” “His gall is the [His] great intestine is the breadth of the great [bitterness is the ruler]…” and truncated endings “His feet are his [soles]”. The spiritual reading explicitly flags: “heavily fragmented… clauses incomplete or displaced… textually broken and uncertain.” Removing lines would not restore a different voice; the same body-map continues.

findings.diagnosis: Mixed/garbled seam: a functional conclusion (“harmonised…”) is abruptly interrupted by an administrative-style inventory of named salvific beings/roles (“Living Spirit… Ambassador… five sleepless guardians”) that do not participate in the immediate body-correspondence narrative. Likely a small insertion at a summary point.
findings.evidence: Text: “This is how each of the worlds have been harmonised (?). Five gods are fastened in him…” then the line collapses into a compressed list: “also the Living Spirit and the Ambassador… the five sleepless guardians.” The spiritual reading notes the exact stumble: “List… is abrupt; functions inferred… naming… compressed and difficult.” This is characteristic of a seam where a systematizer drops in a roster rather than continuing the functional mapping.
findings.scope: Excise the abrupt roster tail in ¶13: “also] the Living Spirit and the Ambassador [yet] the five sleepless guardians.”

findings.diagnosis: Major administrative intrusion into a correspondential chapter: a jurisdictional catalogue of named rulers/camps/firmaments (‘Keeper of Splendour’, ‘King of Honour’, ‘Adamant of Light’, ‘King of Glory’, ‘Porter’) with territorial placements and authority language. It breaks the functional ‘cosmic man’ teaching and anticipates the later ‘watch-district’ narrative by installing an official hierarchy at the seam.
findings.evidence: Text is dominated by appointments/placements: “He has set over him the Keeper of Splendour… camp of the great King of Honour… third firmament… fifth firmament… appointed the King of Glory… authority over the three images… the Porter…” (¶14). This is governance by jurisdiction, not correspondence by function. The spiritual reading flags it as exceptional: “textually chaotic with interrupted titles and placements… sequence… descending governance,” i.e., the reader had to impose a degree-architecture to make it work—classic symptom of an inserted administrative list in a functional discourse.
findings.scope: Excise all of ¶14 (the entire appointment/jurisdiction catalogue beginning “He has [set over him] the Keeper of Splendour…” through “below the three earths]”).

findings.diagnosis: Expansion/addendum in administrative mode that systematizes the hierarchy and institutional mechanism (summons/obedience; sons lists; christological/anthropos identifications), bridging into the later watch-district narrative. Functions can be allegorized, but the voice is institutional and taxonomic, not organic correspondence.
findings.evidence: Text: “refined… five intellectuals of life… the summons and the obedience… six sons… six sons…” (¶15); “placed… the great Mind… Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man” (¶16); “Jesus the Youth was set there…” (¶17); then the administrative aim: “He has made strong these camps… ordinances… circuit of his watch-district” (¶18). The spiritual reading repeatedly notes it is forcing numerology and names into ‘functional’ renderings: “‘six sons’… treated as fullness… exact numerology uncertain,” and for ¶17 “named figure… translated by function.” That is exactly the symptom of a later didactic layer recasting the teaching into Mani’s administrative/register style (camps, ordinances, summons/obedience, named hypostases).
findings.scope: Excise ¶15-18 in full: from “Furthermore: The Ambassador refined…” (¶15) through “neither uprising nor treachery are made in his watch-district.” (¶18).

findings.diagnosis: Coherent narrative block in administrative ‘watch-district’ voice (cosmic governance and rebellions) that now functions as a self-contained exemplum supporting the microcosm analogy. Even though administrative, it is not a small insertion inside a functional paragraph; it is a continuous story unit. Best treated as an overlay block rather than carved up.
findings.evidence: Repeated administrative markers: “camp,” “watch-district,” “watchers,” “authority,” “province/watch” (¶19-29). The spiritual reading reports strong narrative coherence here (“another province falls… remedial descent… completes the descent… generalizes the lesson”). This indicates not random corruption but a stable secondary didactic layer. Removing pieces would damage the internal story logic; yet the whole block differs in teaching mode from the later correspondential psychology (¶35ff).
findings.scope: Annotate ¶19-29 as an administrative overlay exemplum (watch-district/camp rebellion cycle with named officials and mythic episodes) supporting the analogy to the body in ¶30-31.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential return to the chapter’s opening questions: macrocosm disturbances are applied to the body; accommodation (‘taproot’) answers infinity-in-finitude. This is functional analogy rather than roster.
findings.evidence: Text: “So also is this body! A mighty power lives here…” (¶30) and “So, also, is the watch-district of the Mind, which is the body of the flesh” (¶31) and the functional accommodation image “like trees holding to their taproot” (¶33). The spiritual reading shows no forced inference here; it reads as the intended application section.

findings.diagnosis: Core substrate correspondential psychology/regeneration teaching: fivefold binding of soul faculties, fivefold replacement, formation of ‘new man’, virtues mapped explicitly to faculties. This is the chapter’s strongest functional backbone.
findings.evidence: Text is explicitly functional and internally mapped: “It bound the mind in bone… thought in sinew… insight in vein… counsel in flesh… consideration in skin” (¶35); reversal by the Light Mind (¶38-40); direct functional identifications “mind, which is love… thought, which is faith… insight… perfection… counsel… patience… wisdom…” (¶40). The spiritual reading notes explicit textual equating here and treats it as stable.

findings.diagnosis: Clean conclusion tying back to the earlier exemplum and answering invisibility/purity/smallness by analogy and by perceptive ‘eye’. Some discontinuity in numbering (43→51; missing 56) is external to the teaching voice and does not indicate an insertion here.
findings.evidence: Text: “have I taught you… how confusion shall arise in the zone… so… in the camps of the Light Mind” (¶51); “not visible” (¶52); “become small, to the measure of the task” (¶53); “not defiled” (¶54); “mighty… activity… shuts off deliberations” (¶55); “Whoever has an open… eye… can appear” (¶57). The spiritual reading reports smooth closure and explicit return to initial questions.

textual_criticism.summary: Issues found: 4. (1) Genuine damage: ¶11-12 (no action). (2) Small seam insertion: ¶13 roster tail (excise). (3) Large administrative intrusions/expansions at a seam: ¶14 and ¶15-18 (excise). (4) Coherent administrative overlay exemplum: ¶19-29 (annotate, do not carve). Clean substrate confirmations: ¶1-6, ¶9-10, ¶30-33, ¶35-43, ¶51-55/57.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: You have told us that the Light Mi[nd] is this one who shall come and assume the saints. [You sai]d it to us like this: He too is one among the gods [and] many gods are with him. You have also told us: [W]hen he enters withi[n the body of] the flesh and binds the ol[d ma]n with his five counsels, he [set]s his five [couns]els upon him in the five limbs [of his] body.
[So], no[w], where is he? In that the old man is chained in the body! For I see how rebellions arise there despite his bondage, from time to time.
Also, secondly, I a[s]k you: If then he is a great God, unchanging and immeasurable, how could he come and appear in the smallness of the bo[dy]?
The third thing I want you to recount to [me the third thing] a holy one is the Mind, and he is pure; [how could he enter and not be defiled by] the defilement of this body?
Fourthly: If truly the Light Mind exists in [the s]aints, why is his likeness not displayed to us, the way that he is?
The fifth thing I want, for you to tell me and explain about your apostola[te]. Look, it is not clear to me! For they oppress and persecute you in the world.
All that you have unveiled you have [declared] in our presence. Yet, I wanted to kno[w also about the] L[igh]t Mind, the way that he is.

If I shall repeat [again] to you about these things that you are so set upon, and they become true f[o]r you after you are so set upon them, will you understand what you [seek]? On your account I will give vision to they who see! I will make the living fountain overflow for the thirsty, that they may drink and liv[e].

All the error, when the en[e]my of the lights constructed it, he constructed after the likeness of a man. The head of the universe is the beginning of the garments. [H]is neck is the nape of the garm[ents]. His stomach is the five unfolded ones (?), which a[the foundation] of the garm[e]nts. His ribs are all the firmament[s]. His navel is the sphere of the stars and the signs of the zodiac. And, also, [the par]ts [that] come from his navel to his hip are [the extensions] that come from the sphere t[o the corne]rs of the four worlds. His loins are the th[ree eart]hs that are below [the abysses; they are placed] upon the head of the Porter. His [thighs are the roads from the loins] from the [hip] to the earth upon which the Porter [is stood] firm. His shins and his feet a[are the seas] and the entire zone that belongs [to it]

⟨p.91⟩
His heart is mankind. His liver is the four-footed animals. His lung is the race of birds that [fly in] the air. His spleen is the race of fish that swim in the waters. His kidneys are the world of reptiles that creep [up]on the earth. His outer skin is the wall that [which] surrounds the piercing and the great fire. His [the inner skin is the firmament] the vessels of the great fire. His [entrails are] of darkness. His gall is the [His] great intestine is the breadth of the great [bitterness is the ruler] of the worlds. His veins [firmament] all [the spri]ngs and wells. His e[eyes are the two luminaries] His feet are his [soles]
This is how each of the worlds h[ave been ha]rmonised (?). Five gods are fastened in him. [And] they are his soul and his life [In them] man is a sinner

And look, see! The Keeper of Splendour is set firm in the great mind, in the camp above the prison of the bound ones, for he brings to nothing all the gloom of death. An[d a] treachery came about, and an uprising! The Sin abor[te]d, [it t]angled i]n with the soul. It became mixed with this light that it expelled toward the image of the Ambassador. It went [and it was] in the third firmament that is above the watch-t[ower of] the Keeper of Splendour. From that place also it tangled in with the light. It was detached and came down to that which is dry and that which is moist. It [fashio]ned the trees [up]on the dry (land); but in the sea it immediat[ely] took form and made a great uprising in the sea.

Again, look, see! The great King of Honour, who is the thought, he is in the thi[r]d firmament. He is made [to nothing] with wrath. And an uprising came about! A treachery and a[n] anger happened in his camp. The watchers of heaven, who came down to the earth in his watch-district, they did all the deeds of treachery. They have revealed crafts in the world and have unveiled to people the mysteries of heaven. An uprising came about, and a destruction, on the earth [and great ruin was added] to it.

The Adamant [of Light is insight and] the fulfillment. He is set firm upo[n the camp of the Adamant] and a treachery came about in his camp; the occasion when the abortions fell to the earth. They formed Adam and Eve. They begat them so as to reign through them in the world. They fashioned every object of lust upon the earth. The entire world was filled by their lust.

Once again: In the watch of the great King of Glory, wh[O] is the great counsel, he who exercises authority over the thre[e] wheels. A [dis]turbance came about, and an affliction, for [they were greatly] pained and oppressed in the three earths. After the Ambassador displayed his image, the paths closed to their [ways] their ascent was impeded by them [so that] the w[ind], the water, and the fire ascend on them.

[O]nce again: In the watch of the Porter, he who humiliates [the great uproar and] upr]ising of the abysses below [the earth beneath was] bent, the fastenings underneath were loosened [and all was shaken] in the foundation below.
On account of the earthquake that happened in the watch of the Keeper of Splen[dour], the Pillar of Glory came forth; as it [became] helper of the Keeper of Splendour. It bore up under all [burden]s.

Conversely, because of the treachery and the uprising that happened in the watch of the great King of Honour, which is the watchers who came down to earth from the heavens; four angels were called upon about them. They bound the watche[r]s with an eternal chain, in the prison of the blackened ones (?). [Th]ey obliterated their children from upon the earth.

[Th]en, again, the abortions descended in the watch of the Adamant and begat Adam and Eve; because of that great treachery wh[ich] happened, and the mystery of wickedness, he sent Jesus [the Youth] the prayer of the five sons. He assumed them [in response to] the abortions. He fastened them beneath the [from among] the mind of Adam.

⟨p.94⟩
Also, because of the earthquake that happened in these three earths, and in that the paths were hindered and the springs of wind and water and fire were impeded, Jesus cast himself down. He assumed Eve; and he straightened the tracks of the [win]d, the water, and the fire. He opened the springs for them, and he set [in ord]er the path of their ascent.

Once [again]: Since the earth beneath the Porter was loose[ned from] the fastenings that [had been set] because of this too Jesus went down, assuming [Ev]e until he reached tha[t] place. [H]e set in [or]der and stre[ng]th[ened] the fastenings beneath. He returned, [he came] up to his [own] rest.

Look at all these watches of the zon[e], the ones in which these great gods are master, w[atch]ing over them [in their appointed places]. Uprisings have happened, and treachery, in them. The [earthquake happened] in them from time to time; with a great hum[iliati]on, until they humbled the powers of the enmity.

So also is this body! A mighty power lives here, even if it is small in its stature. Nevertheless, Sin dwells within, and the old man who is lodged in it. Certainly he is cruel, with great cunning; until the Light Mind finds how to humble this body, and drive it [according to] his pleasure.

Just so, in the w[atch-]districts of his great outer brothers, they who are masters in the zone: in them, in the great body, the earthquake and treachery happened from time to time. So, also, is the watch-district of the Mind, which is the body of the flesh. Sin raises [up], from time to time, its agitations in the body.

Now you, understand thus, that the powers of light are good. The beginning and the end are unveiled to them. All that they do is being done with correct judgement. Indeed, because of this they may permit the enmity to initiate error, and do its pleasure for a moment. Then they seize [it at once, and bind it, since] they have acted first with a righteous judgement.

⟨p.95⟩
And [with resp]ect to this other (question) that you have put forward: How may the Light Mind come, this great and honoured mighty one, and assume this little body of the flesh? Again, look, see! These gods, in that [are set in their camps, though they] are great and mighty ones. And each one of them is enclosed and hard pressed in this place wherein he is set; like trees holding to their taproot. So also this is how each one of them has held to his taproot in the world, according to the k[ind] of place in which he is set, bearing up till [the end]
(Sin) bou]nd (the soul) in the five members of the body. It bound the mind in bone; the thought in sinew; the insight in vein; the counsel in flesh; the consideration in ski[n].

(Sin) set f[ast] its five powers: its mind upon the mind of the soul; its thought upon the thought of the soul; its insight upon the insight of the soul; its counsel upon the counsel of the soul; its consider[atio]n upon the consideration of the soul. It placed its five [an]gels and authorities upon the five members of the soul, which it had brought in and bound in the flesh. They [continually speak], pronouncing to the soul and continually leading it on to every evil thi[n]g, to all the sins of lust, to the worship of idols, to erroneous opinions, to humili[ation]; in the humiliation of slavery! As it is set fast, wors[hipping] the things that [are in the world] will not remain; making obeisance [to] idols of wood and gold and silver [and stone] worshipping beasts that are unclean and polluted! They are ugly in their appearances and their forms.

⟨p.96⟩
(The soul) assumed error and forgetfulness. It for[go]t its essence and its race and its kindred; kn[ow]ing not the door of the place to pray to him, nor call up to him. It became hostile to its father [and it became hostile to] itself, being wicked [and to its mother within] its own light [and it extinguished]

The Light Mind comes and finds the soul [in its bonds,] it assuming it in the [body,] its wisdom [and by] he shall become for it [so that] the bonds [power over] members in the body. He shall loosen the m[mind of the soul and relea]se it from the bone. He shall release the th[ought of the soul] from the sinew; and s[o] bind the thought [of the sin in] the sinew. He shall release the insight of the soul from the vei[n]; and so bind the insight of the sin in the vein. [He sh]all loosen the counsel of the soul, and release it from the flesh; and so bind the counsel of the sin in the flesh. He shall release the consideration of the soul from the skin; and bin[d] the consideration of the sin in the skin.

⟨p.97⟩
This is how he shall release the members of the soul, and make them free from the five members of sin. Conversely, these five members of sin, which were loose, he shall bind them.

He shall set right the members of the soul; form and purify them, and construct a new man of them, a child of righteousness. [And] when [he] fashions and const[r]ucts and purifies the new man; then he shall bring forth five great living members out from the five great memb[ers]. And he places them in the members of the new man. He shall place his m[ind], which is love, in the mind of the new man. Also, the th[oug]ht, which is faith, he shall pl[ace in] the thought of the new man; whom he shall purify. His insight, which [is perfection, he shall place] in the insight of the new man. His counsel, which [is] patience, he shall place in his counsel. Also, [w]isdom, which is his consideration, in the consideration of the new m[an]. He shall make the image of the word pure from the word of sin; and he adds to it his word, so that his [utterance] becomes nourisher and strengthener [of the new man]

Now, when he shall perf[ect also the tw]elve members. This [is how he shall perfect] and his wisdom. His [mind] becomes righteous, as he perf[ects the twelve members] While formerly he was running [in the way of error;] but instead of this, now he runs [in righteousness,] his road and his path and his [ascent;] also [he mounts up] to the heights, to the great aeons [and he is joined] thus the old man is bound in the [in the body] and his lust, his [craft,] his foolishness in these five members of the bo[body in his five members] the dark spirit is imprisoned with them in a bond and in severe misery.

Also, the new man reigns by his love, by hi[s] faith, by his perfection, by his patience, and by his wisdom. Yet, his king [is] the Light Mind, he w[ho is] king over the totality. He re[igns] o[ver it according to] his pleasure. While the members [are set fast], thus sin is imprisoned. Still, the Light Mind is king, and an affliction may arise in the body from t[im]e to time.

There are occasions when sin shall mount up with its foolishness; and it disturbs the consideration, and it clouds the wisdom and the understanding of the person. It causes truth to be split into doubt in him, and he utters some foo[li]sh words and some [empty deeds]

[T]hen, have I taught you, and opened your (sg.) [eyes], as to how confusion shall arise in the zo[ne], in the camps of these great mig[hty] gods? Again, this is how disturbance shall come about, from ti[me] to time, in the [camps] of the [Li]ght [M]ind.
So al[so] these watch-keepers, for they are set [as] fi[rm in] the zone, (but) they are not visible. Again, this too is the way of the Light Mind, [for he is] not visible in the body.

Also, [corr]esponding to th[ese] outer [watch-keepers]: in that while they are great, [y]et have they contorted themselves. They have [bent themselves down], they have become small, to the measure of the task that is apportioned to each o[n]e [of t]hem. Again, this too is like the Mind, himse[lf] a great one, and exalted; but he is bent over and [has] become small, to this little worthless [bo]dy.

[Even so] the gods in the outer [z]one: they are transcendent and purified, they are set [f]a[st in] the mingling of the totality, (but) are not defiled. [This too is like the] Light [Mind]. While he is placed in hi[s body of flesh,]

⟨p.100⟩
Again, behold the mightiness and the activity of the Light Mind: how vast he is over all the watch-districts of the body! He stays fast at his camp. He shuts off all deliberations of the body from the beguilements of Sin. He limits them and distributes them out. He sets them down at his pleasure.
I have taught you] the deeds of the [Light] Mind! Whoever has an open and percept[ive] eye, [he can] appear to him. Whoever has not that eye, he can not appear to him.

changes_summary: Applied excisions exactly as recommended by the critic. (Finding 4) In ¶13, excised the abrupt roster tail beginning “also] the Living Spirit and the Ambassador [yet] the five sleepless guardians,” leaving the functional conclusion intact. (Finding 5) Excised all of ¶14 (the full appointment/jurisdiction catalogue). (Finding 6) Excised ¶15–18 in full (the administrative expansion concerning intellectuals, sons lists, and camp/watch-district ordinances). Per rules, ¶19–29 were not altered (Finding 7: annotate only). All other paragraphs unchanged.
